To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) cost optimal classification is possible, (ii) the cost dependent information measure can be used in decision tree induction for this, and (iii) it is more adequate to use this measure than to use cost matrices

(1) the use of cost dependent information for decision making is a promising approach for cost optimal decisions in real life applications, and (2) the use of object dependent costs is a promising approach to improve classification performance for cost dependent decisions.

(1) the use of object dependent costs for misclassifications in decision tree induction is possible, (2) the use of cost matrices for misclassifications is not always appropriate, and (3) CAL5 can be used to convert real valued attributes into intervals for decision tree induction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
decision support systems that are based on decision tree classifiers.
the problem of learning decision trees from data with object dependent costs for class decisions, where the costs are given by real values.
the development of methods for the construction of decision trees with object dependent costs of misclassifications, and their evaluation by means of experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cost dependent decision making is a useful tool in many situations.

the method described is more suitable for cost dependent training objects than the method using cost matrices, if the cost matrices are unknown or the costs of misclassifying a certain object are different from those of other objects.
CAL5 is a good algorithm for building decision trees for classification, if the cost of misclassifications depends on the object and is known.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of object dependent costs in decision making is a promising approach for cost optimal decisions in real applications.
we are able to construct cost dependent decision trees with the algorithm CAL5 using object dependent costs.

we have developed an algorithm which allows to build decision trees with object dependent costs and which is more adequate than the method using cost matrices in case that cost dependent training objects can be obtained.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to learn decision trees with object dependent cost functions.
cost matrices should not be used in learning if cost dependent training data are available.
cost matrices are not sufficient to model the cost of misclassifications and that cost dependent objects are a more powerful tool to model the costs in a decision making process.
